messages:
alex: Heads-up — during onboarding of staging/model-int8-3b I hit a reproducible divergence in long-context runs where outputs go nonsensical right after a RoPE wrap boundary (~64k tokens). Repro steps below; failure shows up reliably when we prefill ~65520 tokens then continue with a short query.

alex: Repro (local harness):
```bash
./tools/run_infer --model=staging/model-int8-3b --prompt=fixtures/longprefill_65k.txt --streaming=false --kv-policy=wrap --seed=42 --max-tokens=32 
```
Logs show identical logits until token ~65519 then sudden token collapse to repeated filler. Dumped KV snapshot before/after and saw index offsets shift by +1 in one shard.

alex: Attaching small excerpts from kvcache_dump: (sanitized)
```
KV_SNAPSHOT prefill: shard0 idx=65518 entries=4f3a...
KV_SNAPSHOT post-step: shard0 idx=65519 entries=4f3a...
KV_SNAPSHOT post-fail: shard0 idx=65520 entries=0000... (zeros)
```

alex: Hypothesis: RoPE phase wrap arithmetic interacting with int8 quantized memcpy/alignment leads to a one-off write on wrap that zeros the tail on some shard alignment. Could be stride/tiling mismatch in the int8 memcpy path.

priya: Ugh. Nice repro. Can you put the raw kvcache dumps + model checksum somewhere? Also which quant recipe did you use (per-channel vs per-tensor)?

alex: Uploaded to s3://redwood-test-buckets/onboard/4298765432/ (pre/post dumps + seed). Using int8-perchannel with symmetric calibration set. Model sha: ad3f9b1.

sam: Quick thought — we've seen similar zeroing when the prefill buffer crosses the GPU memory tile boundary and we use a packed memcpy that assumes even alignment. Could you try forcing byte-aligned copies? Local patch suggestion: in runtime/kv/copy.c change copy_aligned to fallback when ((dst_ptr & 0xF) != 0).

sam: Also can you run with `--kv-mode=reset-on-wrap` (experimental) to see if forcing reset avoids silent zeroing? If that fixes output it's probably a write-over-slab bug.

alex: Ran `--kv-mode=reset-on-wrap` — divergence disappears in 5/5 runs. Problem likely in wrap handling. Full CI trace: https://ci.redwood.infra/builds/4298765432 (passed with reset-on-wrap)

matt: If reset-on-wrap masks the bug we still need perf numbers. Resetting KV at wrap will lose cache benefits. Can you run the same workload with perf counters? Interested in tokens/sec and p99 latency.

alex: Numbers: baseline (no wrap) 210 tok/s, wrap-reset 178 tok/s, so ~15% drop. p99 increases from 12ms to 18ms. Saved in the s3 path above under metrics.json.

priya: Ok good data. For onboarding gate we need: 1) deterministic repro added to model-eval harness 2) a small unit test for copy alignment 3) a model rollback plan for customers using >64k contexts.

sam: I'll open a small PR that adds a unit test to runtime/kv and toggles a safer memcpy path behind a perf flag. If perf hit is unacceptable we can add an autotune knob to select aligned memcpy only when prefill length%tile==bad.

matt: +1. Also let's try a RoPE-rescale workaround: on wrap, multiply phases by linear taper rather than hard reset — may keep continuity without touching memcpy. Worth a quick patch to test quality vs perf tradeoff.

ci-bot: build #76234 for branch fix/kv-wrap-alignment finished: SUCCESS — tests: 243 passed, 7 flaky

alex: Thanks team. Action items: sam to PR (runtime memcpy guard), matt to prototype RoPE taper patch, priya to add onboarding eval case + rollback KB. I'll pin this thread with a short writeup after PR lands.

alex: One more note — observed the issue only with int8-perchannel; int4 staging didn't exhibit the zeroing. Might be alignment interaction with 8-bit word copies.

priya: Good callout. We'll block int8-perchannel for >64k until a fix lands and add regression alert to Optimize.
